review_notes:
I reviewed all of Smoothing.lean (lines 1–124): three theorems, with a pointwise Hölder-type convolution bound, an L∞ semigroup bound, and a smooth representative. I did not open other files, so I can't rule out duplication of these steps elsewhere in the library.

The only recurring pattern is the conversion between `eLpNorm … ∞` and `eLpNormEssSup`. The second theorem uses `eLpNorm_exponent_top` forward to get an a.e. bound. The third uses it backward, after `enorm_ae_le_eLpNormEssSup`, to get a real-valued a.e. bound. The two uses go in opposite directions, and each is a one- or two-line rewrite around existing Mathlib API. That is short routine unfolding, not repeated nontrivial reasoning, so a shared lemma would not meet the rubric.

The Hölder-exponent arithmetic (`hi`, `he`) appears only once in this file. Each theorem's main argument is distinct.
